signals.label: No Message-ID Header
signals.detail: The message carries no Message-ID. Practically all mail from real clients and platforms has one; scripted senders frequently omit it.

signals.label: No Date Header
signals.detail: The message has no Date header, which is required by the mail standards and present on essentially all legitimate mail.

cases.name: Message-ID domain differs from the From domain

signals.label: Message-ID From a Different Domain
signals.detail: The Message-ID was generated by "othercorp.example" while the message claims to be from "example.com". Common and harmless for mail sent through a marketing or CRM platform, so weigh it alongside the other findings.

signals.label: No Message-ID Header
signals.detail: The message carries no Message-ID. Practically all mail from real clients and platforms has one; scripted senders frequently omit it.

signals.label: Sent by a Script, Not a Mail Client
signals.detail: The X-Mailer header identifies PHPMailer ("PHPMailer 6.5"). Bulk senders use platforms; this pattern is typical of a phishing kit or a compromised web host sending directly.

signals.label: No Date Header
signals.detail: The message has no Date header, which is required by the mail standards and present on essentially all legitimate mail.

cases.name: bulk-sender headers count as benign evidence

signals.label: Standard Bulk-Sender Headers Present
signals.detail: The message carries List-Unsubscribe and a Message-ID, the headers a legitimate mailing platform adds. These can be forged, but phishing kits usually do not bother.

cases.name: Re: subject with In-Reply-To plus a DMARC failure looks like thread hijacking

signals.label: Presents as a Thread Reply, But Fails Authentication
signals.detail: The subject and headers present this as a reply within an existing conversation, but the message fails a real authentication check. A genuine continuation of a real thread from the real correspondent should authenticate cleanly — this combination points to a compromised account or a hijacked thread, not ordinary phishing, which has no reason to fake thread continuity at all.

cases.name: authserv-id differs from the origin host of the Received chain

signals.label: No Message-ID Header
signals.detail: The message carries no Message-ID. Practically all mail from real clients and platforms has one; scripted senders frequently omit it.

signals.label: No Date Header
signals.detail: The message has no Date header, which is required by the mail standards and present on essentially all legitimate mail.

signals.label: Authentication-Results Claims a Different Server Than Delivered It
signals.detail: The Authentication-Results header claims to be from "mx.attacker.example", but the message's own delivery chain shows it was actually received by "mx.realcorp.example". A security gateway in the chain can legitimately explain this, but it is also the shape of an Authentication-Results header written by whoever sent the message rather than by a real mail server — this tool has no way to independently verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC itself, so a header claiming a pass from a server the delivery chain doesn't corroborate is worth extra scrutiny.
